classification.difficultyReason: For exactly two matching weekdays, account for all three choices of the unmatched person or exclude the all-same and all-different cases found in the preceding parts.

content.prompt: Three people are asked what day of the week they were born. Assume that all seven days are equally likely for each person and that their birth weekdays are independent. Find the probability that

children.label: a
children.prompt: all three were born on Tuesday.

answer.worked:
Let $T$ be the event that all three were born on Tuesday. Each person has probability $\frac17$ of being born on Tuesday.

$$\begin{align*}P(T)&=\left(\frac17\right)^3\\ P(T)&=\frac1{343}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: all three were born on the same day of the week.

answer.worked:
The first person can be born on any day. Each of the next two people must match that day. Let $M$ be the event that all three match.

$$\begin{align*}P(M)&=1\times\frac17\times\frac17\\ P(M)&=\frac1{49}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: all three were born on different days of the week.

answer.worked:
The first person can be born on any day. The second has six available days and the third has five. Let $D$ be the event that all three days differ.

$$\begin{align*}P(D)&=1\times\frac67\times\frac57\\ P(D)&=\frac{30}{49}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: exactly two people were born on the same day of the week.

answer.short:
$\frac{18}{49}$

There are three choices for the person outside the matching pair.
answer.worked:
Choose the person outside the matching pair in $3$ ways. Within the pair, the first day is unrestricted and the second must match. The remaining person's day must differ. Let $E$ be the event that exactly two match.

$$\begin{align*}P(E)&=3\times1\times\frac17\times\frac67\\ P(E)&=\frac{18}{49}\end{align*}$$
